Body.1:
1That man hath perfect blessedness
who walketh not astray
In counsel of ungodly men,
nor stands in sinners' way,
Body.2:
2Nor sitteth in the scorner's chair:
But placeth his delight
Upon GOD's law, and meditates
on his law day and night.
Body.3:
3He shall be like a tree that grows
near planted by a river,
Which in his season yields his fruit,
and his leaf fadeth never:
Body.4:
4And all he doth shall prosper well.
The wicked are not so;
But like they are unto the chaff,
which wind drives to and fro.
Body.5:
5In judgment therefore shall not stand
such as ungodly are;
Nor in th' assembly of the just
shall wicked men appear.
Body.6:
6For why? the way of godly men
unto the LORD is known:
Whereas the way of wicked men
shall quite be overthrown.

Body.1:
1Why rage the heathen? and vain things
why do the people mind?
Kings of the earth do set themselves,
and princes are combined,
Body.2:
2To plot against the LORD, and his
Anointed, saying thus,
Let us asunder break their bands,
and cast their cords from us.
Body.3:
3He that in heaven sits shall laugh;
the Lord shall scorn them all.
Then shall he speak to them in wrath,
in rage he vex them shall.
Body.4:
4Yet, notwithstanding, I have him
to be my King appointed;
And over Zion, my holy hill,
I have him King anointed.
Body.5:
5The sure decree I will declare;
the LORD hath said to me,
Thou art mine only Son; this day
I have begotten thee.
Body.6:
6Ask of me, and for heritage
the heathen I'll make thine;
And, for possession, I to thee
will give earth's utmost line.
Body.7:
7Thou shalt, as with a weighty rod
of iron, break them all;
And, as a potter's sherd, thou shalt
them dash in pieces small.
Body.8:
8Now, therefore, kings, be wise; be taught,
ye judges of the earth:
Serve GOD in fear, and see that ye
join trembling with your mirth.
Body.9:
9Kiss ye the Son, lest in his ire
ye perish from the way,
If once his wrath begin to burn:
bless'd all that on him stay.

Body.1:
1O LORD, how are my foes increased?
against me many rise.
Many say of my soul, For him
in God no succour lies.
Body.2:
2Yet thou my strength and glory art,
th' uplifter of mine head.
I cried, and, from his holy hill,
the LORD me answer made.
Body.3:
3I laid me down and slept, I waked;
for GOD sustained me.
I will not fear though thousands ten
set round against me be.
Body.4:
4Arise, O LORD; save me, my God;
for thou my foes hast stroke
All on the cheek-bone, and the teeth
of wicked men hast broke.
Body.5:
5Salvation doth appertain
unto the LORD alone:
Thy blessing, Lord, for evermore
thy people is upon.

Body.1:
1Give ear unto me when I call,
God of my righteousness:
Have mercy, hear my prayer; thou hast
enlarged me in distress.
Body.2:
2O ye the sons of men! how long
will ye love vanities?
How long my glory turn to shame,
and will ye follow lies?
Body.3:
3But know, that for himself the LORD
the godly man doth choose:
The LORD, when I on him do call,
to hear will not refuse.
Body.4:
4Fear, and sin not; talk with your heart
on bed, and silent be.
Off'rings present of righteousness,
and in the LORD trust ye.
Body.5:
5O who will show us any good?
is that which many say:
But of thy countenance the light,
LORD, lift on us alway.
Body.6:
6Upon my heart, bestowed by thee,
more gladness I have found
Than they, ev'n then, when corn and wine
did most with them abound.
Body.7:
7I will both lay me down in peace,
and quiet sleep will take;
Because thou only me to dwell
in safety, LORD, dost make.

Body.1:
1Give ear unto my words, O LORD,
my meditation weigh.
Hear my loud cry, my King, my God;
for I to thee will pray.
Body.2:
2LORD, thou shalt early hear my voice:
I early will direct
My prayer to thee; and, looking up,
an answer will expect.
Body.3:
3For thou art not a God that doth
in wickedness delight;
Neither shall evil dwell with thee,
nor fools stand in thy sight.
Body.4:
4All that ill-doers are thou hat'st;
cutt'st off that liars be:
The bloody and deceitful man
abhorred is by thee.
Body.5:
5But I into thy house will come
in thine abundant grace;
And I will worship in thy fear
toward thy holy place.
Body.6:
6Because of those mine enemies,
LORD, in thy righteousness
Do thou me lead; do thou thy way
make straight before my face.
Body.7:
7For in their mouth there is no truth,
their inward part is ill;
Their throat's an open sepulchre,
their tongue doth flatter still.
Body.8:
8O God, destroy them; let them be
by their own counsel quelled:
Them for their many sins cast out,
for they 'gainst thee rebelled.
Body.9:
9But let all joy that trust in thee,
and still make shouting noise;
For them thou sav'st: let all that love
thy name in thee rejoice.
Body.10:
10For, LORD, unto the righteous man
thou wilt thy blessing yield:
With favour thou wilt compass him
about, as with a shield.

Body.1:
1LORD, in thy wrath rebuke me not;
Nor in thy hot rage chasten me.
LORD, pity me, for I am weak:
Heal me, for my bones vexed be.
Body.3:
3Because those that deceased are
Of thee shall no remembrance have;
And who is he that will to thee
Give praises lying in the grave?
Body.4:
4I with my groaning weary am,
I also all the night my bed
Have caused for to swim; and I
With tears my couch have watered.
Body.5:
5Mine eye, consumed with grief, grows old,
Because of all mine enemies.
Hence from me, wicked workers all;
For GOD hath heard my weeping cries.
Body.6:
6GOD hath my supplication heard,
My prayer received graciously.
Shamed and sore vexed be all my foes,
Shamed and back turned suddenly.

Body.1:
1In thy great indignation,
O LORD, rebuke me not;
Nor on me lay thy chastening hand
in thy displeasure hot.
Body.2:
2LORD, I am weak, therefore on me
have mercy, and me spare:
Heal me, O LORD, because thou know'st
my bones much vexed are.
Body.3:
3My soul is vexed sore: but, LORD,
how long stay wilt thou make?
Return, LORD, free my soul; and save
me for thy mercies' sake.
Body.4:
4Because of thee in death there shall
no more remembrance be:
Of those that in the grave do lie,
who shall give thanks to thee?
Body.5:
5I with my groaning weary am,
and all the night my bed
I caused for to swim; with tears
my couch I watered.
Body.6:
6By reason of my vexing grief
mine eye consumed is;
It waxeth old, because of all
that be mine enemies.
Body.7:
7But now, depart from me, all ye
that work iniquity:
For why? the LORD hath heard my voice,
when I did mourn and cry.
Body.8:
8Unto my supplication
the LORD did hearing give:
When I to him my prayer make,
the LORD will it receive.
Body.9:
9Let all be shamed and troubled sore,
that en'mies are to me;
Let them turn back, and suddenly
ashamed let them be.

Body.1:
1O LORD my God, in thee do I
my confidence repose:
Save and deliver me from all
my persecuting foes;
Body.2:
2Lest that the enemy my soul
should, like a lion, tear,
In pieces rending it, while there
is no deliverer.
Body.3:
3O LORD my God, if it be so
that I committed this;
If it be so that in my hands
iniquity there is:
Body.5:
5Then let the foe pursue and take
my soul, and my life thrust
Down to the earth, and let him lay
mine honour in the dust.
Body.6:
6Rise in thy wrath, LORD, raise thyself,
for my foes raging be;
And, to the judgment which thou hast
commanded, wake for me.
Body.7:
7So shall th' assembly of thy folk
about encompass thee:
Thou therefore, for their sakes, return
unto thy place on high.
Body.8:
8The LORD he shall the people judge:
my judge, JEHOVAH, be,
After my righteousness, and mine
integrity in me.
Body.9:
9O let the wicked's malice end;
but stablish stedfastly
The righteous: for the righteous God
the hearts and reins doth try.
Body.10:
10In God, who saves th' upright in heart,
is my defence and stay.
God just men judgeth, God is wroth
with ill men ev'ry day.
Body.11:
11If he do not return again,
then he his sword will whet;
His bow he hath already bent,
and hath it ready set:
Body.12:
12He also hath for him prepared
the instruments of death;
Against the persecutors he
his shafts ordained hath.
Body.13:
13Behold, he with iniquity
doth travail, as in birth;
A mischief he conceived hath,
and falsehood shall bring forth.
Body.14:
14He made a pit, and digged it deep,
another there to take;
But he is fall'n into the ditch
which he himself did make.
Body.15:
15Upon his own head his mischief
shall be returned home;
His vi'lent dealing also down
on his own pate shall come.
Body.16:
16According to his righteousness
the LORD I'll magnify;
And will sing praise unto the name
of GOD that is most high.

Body.1:
1How excellent in all the earth,
LORD, our Lord, is thy name!
Who hast thy glory far advanced
above the starry frame.
Body.2:
2From infants' and from sucklings' mouth
thou didest strength ordain,
For thy foes' cause, that so thou might'st
th' avenging foe restrain.
Body.3:
3When I look up unto the heav'ns,
which thine own fingers framed,
Unto the moon, and to the stars,
which were by thee ordained;
Body.4:
4Then say I, What is man, that he
remembered is by thee?
Or what the son of man, that thou
so kind to him should'st be?
Body.5:
5For thou a little lower hast
him than the angels made;
With glory and with dignity
thou crowned hast his head.
Body.7:
7Fowls of the air, fish of the sea,
all that pass through the same.
How excellent in all the earth,
LORD, our Lord, is thy name!

Body.1:
1LORD, thee I'll praise with all my heart,
thy wonders all proclaim.
In thee, Most High, I'll greatly joy,
and sing unto thy name.
Body.2:
2When back my foes were turned, they fell,
and perished at thy sight:
For thou maintain'dst my right and cause;
on throne sat'st judging right.
Body.3:
3The heathen thou rebuked hast,
the wicked overthrown;
Thou hast put out their names, that they
may never more be known.
Body.4:
4O en'my! now destructions have
an end perpetual:
Thou cities razed, perished with them
is their memorial.
Body.5:
5GOD shall endure for aye; he doth
for judgment set his throne;
In righteousness to judge the world,
justice to give each one.
Body.6:
6GOD also will a refuge be
for those that are oppressed;
A refuge will he be in times
of trouble to distressed.
Body.7:
7And they that know thy name, in thee
their confidence will place:
For thou hast not forsaken them
that truly seek thy face.
Body.8:
8O sing ye praises to the LORD
that dwells in Zion hill;
And all the nations among
his deeds record ye still.
Body.9:
9When he enquireth after blood,
he then rememb'reth them:
The humble folk he not forgets
that call upon his name.
Body.11:
11That I, in Zion's daughters' gates,
may all thy praise advance;
And that I may rejoice always
in thy deliverance.
Body.12:
12The heathen are sunk in the pit
which they themselves prepared;
And in the net which they have hid
their own feet fast are snared.
Body.13:
13The LORD is by the judgment known
which he himself hath wrought:
The sinners' hands do make the snares
wherewith themselves are caught.
Body.14:
14They who are wicked into hell
each one shall turned be;
And all the nations that forget
to seek the Lord most high.
Body.15:
15For they that needy are shall not
forgotten be alway;
The expectation of the poor
shall not be lost for aye.
Body.16:
16Arise, LORD, let not man prevail;
judge heathen in thy sight:
That they may know themselves but men,
the nations, LORD, affright.

Body.1:
1Wherefore is it that thou, O LORD,
dost stand from us afar?
And wherefore hidest thou thyself
when times so troublous are?
Body.2:
2The wicked in his loftiness
doth persecute the poor:
In these devices they have framed
let them be taken sure.
Body.3:
3The wicked of his heart's desire
doth talk with boasting great;
He blesseth him that's covetous,
whom yet the LORD doth hate.
Body.4:
4The wicked, through his pride of face,
on God he doth not call;
And in the counsels of his heart
the Lord is not at all.
Body.5:
5His ways they always grievous are;
thy judgments from his sight
Removed are: at all his foes
he puffeth with despite.
Body.6:
6Within his heart he thus hath said,
I shall not moved be;
And no adversity at all
shall ever come to me.
Body.7:
7His mouth with cursing, fraud, deceit,
is filled abundantly;
And underneath his tongue there is
mischief and vanity.
Body.8:
8He closely sits in villages;
he slays the innocent:
Against the poor that pass him by
his cruel eyes are bent.
Body.10:
10Himself he humbleth very low,
he croucheth down withal,
That so a multitude of poor
may by his strong ones fall.
Body.11:
11He thus hath said within his heart,
The Lord hath quite forgot;
He hides his countenance, and he
for ever sees it not.
Body.12:
12O LORD, do thou arise; O God,
lift up thine hand on high:
Put not the meek afflicted ones
out of thy memory.
Body.13:
13Why is it that the wicked man
thus doth the Lord despise?
Because that God will it require
he in his heart denies.
Body.14:
14Thou hast it seen; for their mischief
and spite thou wilt repay:
The poor commits himself to thee;
thou art the orphan's stay.
Body.15:
15The arm break of the wicked man,
and of the evil one;
Do thou seek out his wickedness,
until thou findest none.
Body.16:
16The LORD is king through ages all,
ev'n to eternity;
The heathen people from his land
are perished utterly.
Body.18:
18To judge the fatherless, and those
that are oppressed sore;
That man, that is but sprung of earth,
may them oppress no more.

Body.1:
1I in the LORD do put my trust:
how is it then that ye
Say to my soul, Flee, as a bird,
unto your mountain high?
Body.2:
2For, lo, the wicked bend their bow,
their shafts on string they fit,
That those who upright are in heart
they privily may hit.
Body.3:
3If the foundations be destroyed,
what hath the righteous done?
GOD in his holy temple is,
in heaven is his throne:
Body.4:
4His eyes do see, his eyelids try
men's sons. The just he proves:
But his soul hates the wicked man,
and him that vi'lence loves.
Body.5:
5Snares, fire and brimstone, furious storms,
on sinners he shall rain:
This, as the portion of their cup,
doth unto them pertain.
Body.6:
6Because the LORD most righteous doth
in righteousness delight;
And with a pleasant countenance
beholdeth the upright.

Body.1:
1Help, LORD, because the godly man
doth daily fade away;
And from among the sons of men
the faithful do decay.
Body.2:
2Unto his neighbour everyone
doth utter vanity:
They with a double heart do speak,
and lips of flattery.
Body.3:
3GOD shall cut off all flatt'ring lips,
tongues that speak proudly thus,
We'll with our tongue prevail, our lips
are ours: who's lord o'er us?
Body.4:
4For poor oppressed, and for the sighs
of needy, rise will I,
Saith GOD, and him in safety set
from such as him defy.
Body.5:
5The words of GOD are words most pure;
they be like silver tried
In earthen furnace, seven times
that hath been purified.
Body.6:
6LORD, thou shalt them preserve and keep
for ever from this race.
On each side walk the wicked, when
vile men are high in place.

Body.1:
1How long wilt thou forget me, LORD?
shall it for ever be?
O how long shall it be that thou
wilt hide thy face from me?
Body.2:
2How long take counsel in my soul,
still sad in heart, shall I?
How long exalted over me
shall be mine enemy?
Body.3:
3O LORD my God, consider well,
and answer to me make:
Mine eyes enlighten, lest the sleep
of death me overtake:
Body.4:
4Lest that mine enemy should say,
Against him I prevailed;
And those that trouble me rejoice,
when I am moved and failed.
Body.5:
5But I have all my confidence
thy mercy set upon;
My heart within me shall rejoice
in thy salvation.
Body.6:
6I will unto the LORD my God
sing praises cheerfully,
Because he hath his bounty shown
to me abundantly.

Body.1:
1That there is not a God, the fool
doth in his heart conclude:
They are corrupt, their works are vile;
not one of them doth good.
Body.2:
2Upon men's sons the LORD from heav'n
did cast his eyes abroad,
To see if any understood,
and did seek after God.
Body.3:
3They altogether filthy are,
they all aside are gone;
And there is none that doeth good,
yea, sure there is not one.
Body.4:
4These workers of iniquity
do they not know at all,
That they my people eat as bread,
and on GOD do not call?
Body.5:
5There fear'd they much; for God is with
the whole race of the just.
You shame the counsel of the poor,
because GOD is his trust.
Body.6:
6Let Isr'el's help from Zion come:
when back the LORD shall bring
His captives, Jacob shall rejoice,
and Israel shall sing.

Body.1:
1Within thy tabernacle, LORD,
who shall abide with thee?
And in thy high and holy hill
who shall a dweller be?
Body.2:
2The man that walketh uprightly,
and worketh righteousness,
And as he thinketh in his heart,
so doth he truth express.
Body.3:
3Who doth not slander with his tongue,
nor to his friend doth hurt;
Nor yet against his neighbour doth
take up an ill report.
Body.4:
4In whose eyes vile men are despised;
but those that GOD do fear
He honoureth; and changeth not,
though to his hurt he swear.
Body.5:
5His coin puts not to usury,
nor take reward will he
Against the guiltless. Who doth thus
shall never moved be.

Body.1:
1Lord, keep me; for I trust in thee.
To GOD thus was my speech,
Thou art my Lord; and unto thee
my goodness doth not reach:
Body.2:
2To saints on earth, to th' excellent,
where my delight's all placed.
Their sorrows shall be multiplied
to other gods that haste:
Body.3:
3Of their drink-offerings of blood
I will no off'ring make;
Yea, neither I their very names
up in my lips will take.
Body.4:
4GOD is of mine inheritance
and cup the portion;
The lot that fallen is to me
thou dost maintain alone.
Body.5:
5Unto me happily the lines
in pleasant places fell;
Yea, the inheritance I got
in beauty doth excel.
Body.6:
6I bless the LORD, because he doth
by counsel me conduct;
And in the seasons of the night
my reins do me instruct.
Body.7:
7Before me still the LORD I set:
sith it is so that he
Doth ever stand at my right hand,
I shall not moved be.
Body.8:
8Because of this my heart is glad,
and joy shall be expressed
Ev'n by my glory; and my flesh
in confidence shall rest.
Body.9:
9Because my soul in grave to dwell
shall not be left by thee;
Nor wilt thou give thine Holy One
corruption to see.
Body.10:
10Thou wilt me show the path of life:
of joys there is full store
Before thy face; at thy right hand
are pleasures evermore.

Body.1:
1LORD, hear the right, attend my cry,
unto my pray'r give heed,
That doth not in hypocrisy
from feigned lips proceed.
Body.2:
2And from before thy presence forth
my sentence do thou send:
Toward these things that equal are
do thou thine eyes intend.
Body.3:
3Thou prov'dst mine heart, thou visit'dst me
by night, thou didst me try,
Yet nothing found'st; for that my mouth
shall not sin, purposed I.
Body.4:
4As for men's works, I, by the word
that from thy lips doth flow,
Did me preserve out of the paths
wherein destroyers go.
Body.5:
5Hold up my goings, Lord, me guide
in those thy paths divine,
So that my footsteps may not slide
out of those ways of thine.
Body.6:
6I called have on thee, O God,
because thou wilt me hear:
That thou may'st hearken to my speech,
to me incline thine ear.
Body.7:
7Thy wondrous loving-kindness show,
thou that, by thy right hand,
Sav'st them that trust in thee from those
that up against them stand.
Body.8:
8As th' apple of the eye me keep;
in thy wings' shade me close
From lewd oppressors, compassing
me round, as deadly foes.
Body.9:
9In their own fat they are inclosed;
their mouth speaks loftily.
Our steps they compassed; and to ground
down bowing set their eye.
Body.10:
10He like unto a lion is
that's greedy of his prey,
Or lion young, which lurking doth
in secret places stay.
Body.11:
11Arise, and disappoint my foe,
and cast him down, O LORD:
My soul save from the wicked man,
the man which is thy sword.
Body.12:
12From men, which are thy hand, O LORD,
from worldly men me save,
Which only in this present life
their part and portion have.
Body.13:
13Whose belly with thy treasure hid
thou fill'st: they children have
In plenty; of their goods the rest
they to their children leave.
Body.14:
14But as for me, I thine own face
in righteousness will see;
And with thy likeness, when I wake,
I satisfied shall be.

Body.1:
1Thee will I love, O LORD, my strength.
My fortress is the LORD,
My rock, and he that doth to me
deliverance afford:
Body.2:
2My God, my strength, whom I will trust,
a buckler unto me,
The horn of my salvation,
and my high tow'r, is he.
Body.3:
3Upon the LORD, who worthy is
of praises, will I cry;
And then shall I preserved be
safe from mine enemy.
Body.5:
5In my distress I called on God,
cry to my God did I;
He from his temple heard my voice,
to his ears came my cry.
Body.6:
6Th' earth, as affrighted, then did shake,
trembling upon it seized:
The hills' foundations moved were,
because he was displeased.
Body.7:
7Up from his nostrils came a smoke,
and from his mouth there came
Devouring fire, and coals by it
were turned into flame.
Body.8:
8He also bowed down the heav'ns,
and thence he did descend;
And thickest clouds of darkness did
under his feet attend.
Body.9:
9And he upon a cherub rode,
and thereon he did fly;
Yea, on the swift wings of the wind
his flight was from on high.
Body.10:
10He darkness made his secret place:
about him, for his tent,
Dark waters were, and thickest clouds
of th' airy firmament.
Body.11:
11And at the brightness of that light,
which was before his eye,
His thick clouds passed away, hailstones
and coals of fire did fly.
Body.12:
12The LORD God also in the heav'ns
did thunder in his ire;
And there the Highest gave his voice,
hailstones and coals of fire.
Body.13:
13Yea, he his arrows sent abroad,
and them he scattered;
His lightnings also he shot out,
and them discomfited.
Body.14:
14The waters' channels then were seen,
the world's foundations vast
At thy rebuke discovered were,
and at thy nostrils' blast.
Body.15:
15And from above the Lord sent down,
and took me from below;
From many waters he me drew,
which would me overflow.
Body.16:
16He me relieved from my strong foes,
and such as did me hate;
Because he saw that they for me
too strong were, and too great.
Body.17:
17They me prevented in the day
of my calamity;
But even then the LORD himself
a stay was unto me.
Body.18:
18He to a place where liberty
and room was hath me brought;
Because he took delight in me,
he my deliv'rance wrought.
Body.19:
19According to my righteousness
he did me recompense,
He me repaid according to
my hands' pure innocence.
Body.20:
20For I GOD's ways kept, from my God
did not turn wickedly.
  His judgments were before me, I
his laws put not from me.
Body.22:
22After my righteousness the LORD
hath recompensed me,
After the cleanness of my hands
appearing in his eye.
Body.23:
23Thou gracious to the gracious art,
to upright men upright:
Pure to the pure, froward thou kyth'st
unto the froward wight.
Body.24:
24For thou wilt the afflicted save
in grief that low do lie:
But wilt bring down the countenance
of them whose looks are high.
Body.25:
25The LORD will light my candle so,
that it shall shine full bright:
The LORD my God will also make
my darkness to be light.
Body.26:
26By thee through troops of men I break,
and them discomfit all;
And, by my God assisting me,
I overleap a wall.
Body.27:
27As for God, perfect is his way:
the LORD his word is tried;
He is a buckler to all those
who do in him confide.
Body.28:
28Who but the LORD is God? but he
who is a rock and stay?
'Tis God that girdeth me with strength,
and perfect makes my way.
Body.29:
29He made my feet swift as the hinds,
set me on my high places.
Mine hands to war he taught, mine arms
brake bows of steel in pieces.
Body.30:
30The shield of thy salvation
thou didst on me bestow:
Thy right hand held me up, and great
thy kindness made me grow.
Body.31:
31And in my way my steps thou hast
enlarged under me,
That I go safely, and my feet
are kept from sliding free.
Body.32:
32Mine en'mies I pursued have,
and did them overtake;
Nor did I turn again till I
an end of them did make.
Body.34:
34And thou hast giv'n to me the necks
of all mine enemies;
That I might them destroy and slay,
who did against me rise.
Body.35:
35They cried out, but there was none
that would or could them save;
Yea, they did cry unto the LORD,
but he no answer gave.
Body.36:
36Then did I beat them small as dust
before the wind that flies;
And I did cast them out like dirt
upon the street that lies.
Body.37:
37Thou mad'st me free from people's strife,
and heathen's head to be:
A people whom I have not known
shall service do to me.
Body.38:
38At hearing they shall me obey,
to me they shall submit.
Strangers for fear shall fade away,
who in close places sit.
Body.39:
39GOD lives, bless'd be my Rock; the God
of my health praised be.
God doth avenge me, and subdues
the people under me.
Body.40:
40He saves me from mine enemies;
yea, thou hast lifted me
Above my foes; and from the man
of vi'lence set me free.
Body.41:
41Therefore to thee will I give thanks
the heathen folk among;
And to thy name, O LORD, I will
sing praises in a song.
Body.42:
42He great deliv'rance gives his king:
he mercy doth extend
To David, his anointed one,
and his seed without end.

Body.1:
1The heav'ns God's glory do declare,
the skies his hand-works preach:
Day utters speech to day, and night
to night doth knowledge teach.
Body.2:
2There is no speech nor tongue to which
their voice doth not extend:
Their line is gone through all the earth,
their words to the world's end.
Body.3:
3In them he set the sun a tent;
Who, bridegroom-like, forth goes
From's chamber, as a strong man doth
to run his race rejoice.
Body.4:
4From heav'n's end is his going forth,
circling to th' end again;
And there is nothing from his heat
that hidden doth remain.
Body.5:
5GOD's law is perfect, and converts
the soul in sin that lies:
GOD's testimony is most sure,
and makes the simple wise.
Body.6:
6The statutes of the LORD are right,
and do rejoice the heart:
The LORD's command is pure, and doth
light to the eyes impart.
Body.7:
7Unspotted is the fear of GOD,
and doth endure for ever:
The judgments of the LORD are true
and righteous altogether.
Body.8:
8They more than gold, yea, much fine gold,
to be desired are:
Than honey, honey from the comb
that droppeth, sweeter far.
Body.9:
9Moreover, they thy servant warn
how he his life should frame:
A great reward provided is
for them that keep the same.
Body.10:
10Who can his errors understand?
O cleanse thou me within
From secret faults. Thy servant keep
from all presumptuous sin:
Body.11:
11And do not suffer them to have
dominion over me:
Then righteous and innocent
I from much sin shall be.
Body.12:
12The words which from my mouth proceed,
the thoughts sent from my heart,
Accept, O LORD, for thou my strength
and my Redeemer art.

Body.1:
1JEHOVAH hear thee in the day
when trouble he doth send:
And let the name of Jacob's God
thee from all ill defend.
Body.2:
2O let him help send from above,
out of his sanctuary:
From Zion, his own holy hill,
let him give strength to thee.
Body.3:
3Let him remember all thy gifts,
accept thy sacrifice:
Grant thee thine heart's wish, and fulfil
thy thoughts and counsel wise.
Body.4:
4In thy salvation we will joy;
in our God's name we will
Display our banners: and the LORD
thy prayers all fulfil.
Body.5:
5Now know I GOD his king doth save:
he from his holy heav'n
Will hear him, with the saving strength
by his own right hand giv'n.
Body.6:
6In chariots some put confidence,
some horses trust upon:
But we remember will the name
of our LORD God alone.
Body.7:
7We rise, and upright stand, when they
are bowed down, and fall.
Deliver, LORD; and let the King
us hear, when we do call.

Body.1:
1The king in thy great strength, O LORD,
shall very joyful be:
In thy salvation rejoice
how veh'mently shall he!
Body.2:
2Thou hast bestowed upon him
all that his heart would have;
And thou from him didst not withhold
whate'er his lips did crave.
Body.3:
3For thou with blessings him prevent'st
of goodness manifold;
And thou hast set upon his head
a crown of purest gold.
Body.4:
4When he desired life of thee,
thou life to him didst give;
Ev'n such a length of days, that he
for evermore should live.
Body.5:
5In that salvation wrought by thee
his glory is made great;
Honour and comely majesty
thou hast upon him set.
Body.6:
6Because that thou for evermore
most blessed hast him made;
And thou hast with thy countenance
made him exceeding glad.
Body.7:
7Because the king upon the LORD
his confidence doth lay;
And through the grace of the Most High
shall not be moved away.
Body.8:
8Thine hand shall all those men find out
that en'mies are to thee;
Ev'n thy right hand shall find out those
of thee that haters be.
Body.9:
9Like fiery ov'n thou shalt them make,
when kindled is thine ire;
GOD shall them swallow in his wrath,
devour them shall the fire.
Body.10:
10Their fruit from earth thou shalt destroy,
their seed men from among:
For they beyond their might 'gainst thee
did plot mischief and wrong.
Body.11:
11Thou therefore shalt make them turn back,
when thou thy shafts shalt place
Upon thy strings, made ready all
to fly against their face.
Body.12:
12In thy great pow'r and strength, O LORD,
be thou exalted high;
So shall we sing with joyful hearts,
thy power praise shall we.

Body.1:
1My God, my God, why hast thou me
forsaken? why so far
Art thou from helping me, and from
my words that roaring are?
Body.2:
2All day, my God, to thee I cry,
yet am not heard by thee;
And in the season of the night
I cannot silent be.
Body.3:
3But thou art holy, thou that dost
inhabit Isr'el's praise.
Our fathers hoped in thee, they hoped,
and thou didst them release.
Body.4:
4When unto thee they sent their cry,
to them deliv'rance came:
Because they put their trust in thee,
they were not put to shame.
Body.5:
5But as for me, a worm I am,
and as no man am prized:
Reproach of men I am, and by
the people am despised.
Body.7:
7This man did trust in GOD, that he
would free him by his might:
Let him deliver him, sith he
had in him such delight.
Body.8:
8But thou art he out of the womb
that didst me safely take;
When I was on my mother's breasts
thou me to hope didst make.
Body.9:
9And I was cast upon thy care,
ev'n from the womb till now;
And from my mother's belly, Lord,
my God and guide art thou.
Body.10:
10Be not far off, for grief is near,
and none to help is found.
Bulls many compass me, strong bulls
of Bashan me surround.
Body.11:
11Their mouths they opened wide on me,
upon me gape did they,
Like to a lion ravening
and roaring for his prey.
Body.12:
12Like water I'm poured out, my bones
all out of joint do part:
Amidst my bowels, as the wax,
so melted is my heart.
Body.13:
13My strength is like a potsherd dried;
my tongue it cleaveth fast
Unto my jaws; and to the dust
of death thou brought me hast.
Body.14:
14For dogs have compassed me about:
the wicked, that did meet
In their assembly, me inclosed;
they pierced my hands and feet.
Body.15:
15I all my bones may tell; they do
upon me look and stare.
Upon my vesture lots they cast,
and clothes among them share.
Body.16:
16But be not far, O LORD, my strength;
haste to give help to me.
From sword my soul, from pow'r of dogs
my darling set thou free.
Body.17:
17Out of the roaring lion's mouth
do thou me shield and save:
For from the horns of unicorns
an ear to me thou gave.
Body.18:
18I will show forth thy name unto
those that my brethren are;
Amidst the congregation
thy praise I will declare.
Body.19:
19Praise ye the LORD, who do him fear;
him glorify all ye
The seed of Jacob: fear him all
that Isr'el's children be.
Body.20:
20For he despised not nor abhorred
th' afflicted's misery;
Nor from him hid his face, but heard
when he to him did cry.
Body.21:
21Within the congregation great
my praise shall be of thee;
My vows before them that him fear
shall be performed by me.
Body.22:
22The meek shall eat, and shall be filled;
they also praise shall give
Unto the LORD that do him seek:
your heart shall ever live.
Body.23:
23All ends of th' earth remember shall,
and turn the LORD unto;
All kindreds of the nations
to him shall homage do:
Body.24:
24Because the kingdom to the LORD
doth appertain as his;
Likewise among the nations
the Governor he is.
Body.25:
25Earth's fat ones eat, and worship shall:
all who to dust descend
Shall bow to him; none of them can
his soul from death defend.
Body.26:
26A seed shall service do to him;
unto the Lord it shall
Be for a generation
reckoned in ages all.
Body.27:
27They shall come, and they shall declare
his truth and righteousness
Unto a people yet unborn,
and that he hath done this.

Body.1:
1The LORD's my shepherd, I'll not want.
He makes me down to lie
In pastures green: he leadeth me
the quiet waters by.
Body.2:
2My soul he doth restore again;
and me to walk doth make
Within the paths of righteousness,
ev'n for his own name's sake.
Body.3:
3Yea, though I walk in death's dark vale,
yet will I fear none ill:
For thou art with me; and thy rod
and staff me comfort still.
Body.4:
4My table thou hast furnished
in presence of my foes;
My head thou dost with oil anoint,
and my cup overflows.
Body.5:
5Goodness and mercy all my life
shall surely follow me:
And in GOD's house for evermore
my dwelling-place shall be.

Body.1:
1The earth belongs unto the LORD,
and all that it contains;
The world that is inhabited,
and all that there remains.
Body.2:
2For the foundations thereof
he on the seas did lay,
And he hath it established
upon the floods to stay.
Body.3:
3Who is the man that shall ascend
into the hill of GOD?
Or who within his holy place
shall have a firm abode?
Body.4:
4Whose hands are clean, whose heart is pure,
and unto vanity
Who hath not lifted up his soul,
nor sworn deceitfully.
Body.5:
5He from th' ETERNAL shall receive
the blessing him upon,
And righteousness, ev'n from the God
of his salvation.
Body.6:
6This is the generation
that after him enquire,
O Jacob, who do seek thy face
with their whole heart's desire.
Body.7:
7Ye gates, lift up your heads on high;
ye doors that last for aye,
Be lifted up, that so the King
of glory enter may.
Body.8:
8But who of glory is the King?
The mighty LORD is this;
Ev'n that same LORD, that great in might
and strong in battle is.
Body.9:
9Ye gates, lift up your heads; ye doors,
doors that do last for aye,
Be lifted up, that so the King
of glory enter may.
Body.10:
10But who is he that is the King
of glory? who is this?
The LORD of hosts, and none but he,
the King of glory is.

Body.1:
1To thee I lift my soul:
O LORD, I trust in thee:
My God, let me not be asham'd,
nor foes triumph o'er me.
Body.2:
2Let none that wait on thee
be put to shame at all;
But those that without cause transgress,
let shame upon them fall.
Body.3:
3Show me thy ways, O LORD;
thy paths, O teach thou me:
And do thou lead me in thy truth,
therein my teacher be:
Body.4:
4For thou art God that dost
to me salvation send,
And I upon thee all the day
expecting do attend.
Body.5:
5Thy tender mercies, LORD,
I pray thee to remember,
And loving-kindnesses; for they
have been of old for ever.
Body.6:
6My sins and faults of youth
do thou, O LORD, forget:
After thy mercy think on me,
and for thy goodness great.
Body.7:
7GOD good and upright is:
the way he'll sinners show.
The meek in judgment he will guide,
and make his path to know.
Body.8:
8The whole paths of the LORD
are truth and mercy sure,
To those that do his cov'nant keep,
and testimonies pure.
Body.9:
9Now, for thine own name's sake,
O LORD, I thee entreat
To pardon mine iniquity;
for it is very great.
Body.10:
10What man is he that fears
the LORD, and doth him serve?
Him shall he teach the way that he
shall choose, and still observe.
Body.11:
11His soul shall dwell at ease;
and his posterity
Shall flourish still, and of the earth
inheritors shall be.
Body.12:
12With those that fear him is
the secret of the LORD;
The knowledge of his covenant
he will to them afford.
Body.13:
13Mine eyes upon the LORD
continually are set;
For he it is that shall bring forth
my feet out of the net.
Body.14:
14Turn unto me thy face,
and to me mercy show;
Because that I am desolate,
and am brought very low.
Body.15:
15My heart's griefs are increased:
me from distress relieve.
See mine affliction and my pain,
and all my sins forgive.
Body.16:
16Consider thou my foes,
because they many are;
And it a cruel hatred is
which they against me bear.
Body.17:
17O do thou keep my soul,
do thou deliver me:
And let me never be ashamed,
because I trust in thee.
Body.18:
18Let uprightness and truth
keep me, who thee attend.
Redemption, Lord, to Israel
from all his troubles send.

Body.1:
1To thee I lift my soul, O LORD:
my God, I trust in thee:
Let me not be ashamed; let not
my foes triumph o'er me.
Body.2:
2Yea, let thou none ashamed be
that do on thee attend:
Ashamed let them be, O Lord,
who without cause offend.
Body.3:
3Thy ways, LORD, show; teach me thy paths:
lead me in truth, teach me:
For of my safety thou art God;
all day I wait on thee.
Body.4:
4Thy mercies, that most tender are,
do thou, O LORD, remember,
And loving-kindnesses; for they
have been of old for ever.
Body.5:
5Let not the errors of my youth,
nor sins, remembered be:
In mercy, for thy goodness' sake,
O LORD, remember me.
Body.6:
6The LORD is good and gracious,
he upright is also:
He therefore sinners will instruct
in ways that they should go.
Body.7:
7The meek and lowly he will guide
in judgment just alway:
To meek and poor afflicted ones
he'll clearly teach his way.
Body.8:
8The whole paths of the LORD our God
are truth and mercy sure,
To such as keep his covenant,
and testimonies pure.
Body.9:
9Now, for thine own name's sake, O LORD,
I humbly thee entreat
To pardon mine iniquity;
for it is very great.
Body.10:
10What man fears GOD? him shall he teach
the way that he shall choose.
His soul shall dwell at ease; his seed
the earth, as heirs, shall use.
Body.11:
11The secret of the LORD is with
such as do fear his name;
And he his holy covenant
will manifest to them.
Body.12:
12Towards the LORD my waiting eyes
continually are set;
For he it is that shall bring forth
my feet out of the net.
Body.13:
13O turn thee unto me, O God,
have mercy me upon;
Because I solitary am,
and in affliction.
Body.14:
14Enlarged the griefs are of mine heart;
me from distress relieve.
See mine affliction and my pain,
and all my sins forgive.
Body.15:
15Consider thou mine enemies,
because they many are;
And it a cruel hatred is
which they against me bear.
Body.16:
16O do thou keep my soul; O God,
do thou deliver me:
Let me not be ashamed; for I
do put my trust in thee.
Body.17:
17O let integrity and truth
keep me, who thee attend.
Redemption, Lord, to Israel
from all his troubles send.

Body.1:
1Judge me, O LORD, for I have walked
in mine integrity:
I trusted also in the LORD;
slide therefore shall not I.
Body.3:
3With persons vain I have not sat,
nor with dissemblers gone:
Th' assembly of ill men I hate;
to sit with such I shun.
Body.4:
4Mine hands in innocence, O LORD,
I'll wash and purify;
So to thine holy altar go,
and compass it will I:
Body.5:
5That I, with voice of thanksgiving,
may publish and declare,
And tell of all thy mighty works,
that great and wondrous are.
Body.6:
6The habitation of thy house,
LORD, I have loved well;
Yea, in that place I do delight
where doth thine honour dwell.
Body.7:
7With sinners gather not my soul,
and such as blood would spill:
Whose hands mischievous plots, right hand
corrupting bribes do fill.
Body.8:
8But as for me, I will walk on
in mine integrity:
Do thou redeem me, and, O Lord,
be merciful to me.
Body.9:
9My foot upon an even place
doth stand with stedfastness:
Within the congreg"ations
th' ETERNAL I will bless.

Body.1:
1The LORD's my light and saving health,
who shall make me dismayed?
My life's strength is the LORD, of whom
then shall I be afraid?
Body.2:
2When as mine enemies and foes,
most wicked persons all,
To eat my flesh against me rose,
they stumbled and did fall.
Body.3:
3Against me though an host encamp,
my heart yet fearless is:
Though war against me rise, I will
be confident in this.
Body.4:
4One thing I of the LORD desired,
and will seek to obtain,
That all days of my life I may
within GOD's house remain;
Body.5:
5That I the beauty of the LORD
behold may and admire,
And that I in his holy place
may rev'rently enquire.
Body.6:
6For he in his pavilion shall
me hide in evil days;
In secret of his tent me hide,
and on a rock me raise.
Body.7:
7And now, ev'n at this present time,
mine head shall lifted be
Above all those that are my foes,
and round encompass me:
Body.8:
8Therefore unto his tabernacle
I'll sacrifices bring
Of joyfulness; I'll sing, yea, I
to GOD will praises sing.
Body.9:
9O LORD, give ear unto my voice,
when I do cry to thee;
Upon me also mercy have,
and do thou answer me.
Body.10:
10When thou didst say, Seek ye my face,
then unto thee reply
Thus did my heart, Above all things
thy face, LORD, seek will I.
Body.11:
11Far from me hide not thou thy face;
put not away from thee
Thy servant in thy wrath: thou hast
an helper been to me.
Body.12:
12O God of my salvation,
leave me not, nor forsake:
Though me my parents both should leave,
the LORD will me up take.
Body.13:
13O LORD, instruct me in thy way,
to me a leader be
In a plain path, because of those
that hatred bear to me.
Body.14:
14Give me not to mine en'mies' will;
for witnesses that lie
Against me risen are, and such
as breathe out cruelty.
Body.15:
15I fainted had, unless that I
believed had to see
The LORD's own goodness in the land
of them that living be.
Body.16:
16Wait on the LORD, and be thou strong,
and he shall strength afford
Unto thine heart; yea, do thou wait,
I say, upon the LORD.

Body.2:
2The voice hear of my humble pray'rs,
when unto thee I cry;
When to thine holy oracle
I lift mine hands on high.
Body.3:
3With ill men draw me not away
that work iniquity;
That speak peace to their friends, while in
their hearts doth mischief lie.
Body.4:
4Give them according to their deeds
and ills endeavoured:
And as their handiworks deserve,
to them be rendered.
Body.5:
5God shall not build, but them destroy,
who would not understand
The LORD's own works, nor did regard
the doing of his hand.
Body.6:
6For ever blessed be the LORD,
for graciously he heard
The voice of my petitions,
and prayers did regard.
Body.7:
7The LORD's my strength and shield; my heart
upon him did rely;
And I am helped: hence my heart
doth joy exceedingly.
Body.8:
8And with my song I will him praise.
Their strength is GOD alone:
He also is the saving strength
of his anointed one.
Body.9:
9O thine own people do thou save,
bless thine inheritance;
Them also do thou feed, and them
for evermore advance.

Body.1:
1Give ye unto the LORD, ye sons
that of the mighty be,
All strength and glory to the LORD
with cheerfulness give ye.
Body.2:
2Unto the LORD the glory give
that to his name is due;
And in the beauty of holiness
unto JEHOVAH bow.
Body.3:
3The LORD's voice on the waters is;
the God of majesty
Doth thunder, and on multitudes
of waters sitteth he.
Body.4:
4A pow'rful voice it is that comes
out from the LORD most high;
The voice of that great LORD is full
of glorious majesty.
Body.5:
5The voice of the ETERNAL doth
asunder cedars tear;
Yea, God the LORD doth cedars break
that Lebanon doth bear.
Body.6:
6He makes them like a calf to skip,
ev'n that great Lebanon,
And, like to a young unicorn,
the mountain Sirion.
Body.7:
7God's voice divides the flames of fire;
the desert it doth shake:
The LORD doth make the wilderness
of Kadesh all to quake.
Body.8:
8GOD's voice doth make the hinds to calve,
it makes the forest bare:
And in his temple everyone
his glory doth declare.
Body.9:
9The LORD sits on the floods; the LORD
sits King, and ever shall.
The LORD will give his people strength,
and with peace bless them all.

Body.1:
1LORD, I will thee extol, for thou
hast lifted me on high,
And over me thou to rejoice
mad'st not mine enemy.
Body.2:
2O thou who art the LORD my God,
I in distress to thee,
With loud cries lifted up my voice,
and thou hast healed me.
Body.3:
3O LORD, my soul thou hast brought up,
and rescued from the grave;
That I to pit should not go down,
alive thou didst me save.
Body.4:
4O ye that are his holy ones,
sing praise unto the LORD;
And give unto him thanks, when ye
his holiness record.
Body.5:
5For but a moment lasts his wrath;
life in his favour lies:
Weeping may for a night endure,
at morn doth joy arise.
Body.6:
6In my prosperity I said,
that nothing shall me move.
O LORD, thou hast my mountain made
to stand strong by thy love:
Body.7:
7But when that thou, O gracious God,
didst hide thy face from me,
Then quickly was my prosp'rous state
turned into misery.
Body.8:
8Wherefore unto the LORD my cry
I caused to ascend:
My humble supplication
I to the LORD did send.
Body.9:
9What profit is there in my blood,
when I go down to pit?
Shall unto thee the dust give praise?
thy truth declare shall it?
Body.10:
10Hear, LORD, have mercy; help me, LORD:
 Thou turned hast my sadness
To dancing; yea, my sackcloth loosed,
and girded me with gladness;
Body.11:
11That sing thy praise my glory may,
and never silent be.
O LORD my God, for evermore
I will give thanks to thee.

Body.1:
1In thee, O LORD, I put my trust,
shamed let me never be;
According to thy righteousness
do thou deliver me.
Body.2:
2Bow down thine ear to me, with speed
send me deliverance:
To save me, my strong rock be thou,
and my house of defence.
Body.3:
3Because thou art my rock, and thee
I for my fortress take;
Therefore do thou me lead and guide,
ev'n for thine own name's sake.
Body.4:
4And sith thou art my strength, therefore
pull me out of the net,
Which they in subtlety for me
so privily have set.
Body.5:
5Into thine hands I do commit
my spirit: for thou art he,
O thou, JEHOVAH, God of truth,
that hast redeemed me.
Body.6:
6Those that do lying vanities
regard, I have abhorred:
But as for me, my confidence
is fixed on the LORD.
Body.7:
7I'll in thy mercy gladly joy:
for thou my miseries
Considered hast; thou hast my soul
known in adversities:
Body.8:
8And thou hast not inclosed me
within the en'my's hand;
And by thee have my feet been made
in a large room to stand.
Body.9:
9O LORD, upon me mercy have,
for trouble is on me:
Mine eye, my belly, and my soul,
with grief consumed be.
Body.10:
10Because my life with grief is spent,
my years with sighs and groans:
My strength doth fail; and for my sin
consumed are my bones.
Body.11:
11I was a scorn to all my foes,
and to my friends a fear;
And specially reproached of those
that were my neighbours near:
Body.12:
12When they me saw they from me fled.
Ev'n so I am forgot,
As men are out of mind when dead:
I'm like a broken pot.
Body.13:
13For slanders I of many heard;
fear compassed me, while they
Against me did consult, and plot
to take my life away.
Body.14:
14But as for me, O LORD, my trust
upon thee I did lay;
And I to thee, Thou art my God,
did confidently say.
Body.15:
15My times are wholly in thine hand:
do thou deliver me
From their hands that mine enemies
and persecutors be.
Body.16:
16Thy countenance to shine do thou
upon thy servant make:
Unto me give salvation,
for thy great mercies' sake.
Body.17:
17Let me not be ashamed, O LORD,
for on thee called I have:
Let wicked men be shamed, let them
be silent in the grave.
Body.18:
18To silence put the lying lips,
that grievous things do say,
And hard reports, in pride and scorn,
on righteous men do lay.
Body.19:
19How great's the goodness thou for them
that fear thee keep'st in store,
And wrought'st for them that trust in thee
the sons of men before!
Body.20:
20In secret of thy presence thou
shalt hide them from man's pride:
From strife of tongues thou closely shalt,
as in a tent, them hide.
Body.21:
21All praise and thanks be to the LORD;
for he hath magnified
His wondrous love to me within
a city fortified.
Body.22:
22For from thine eyes cut off I am,
I in my haste had said;
My voice yet heard'st thou, when to thee
with cries my moan I made.
Body.23:
23O love the LORD, all ye his saints;
because the LORD doth guard
The faithful, and he plenteously
proud doers doth reward.
Body.24:
24Be of good courage, and he strength
unto your heart shall send,
All ye whose hope and confidence
doth on the LORD depend.

Body.1:
1O blessed is the man to whom
is freely pardoned
All the transgression he hath done,
whose sin is covered.
Body.2:
2Blessed is the man to whom the LORD
imputeth not his sin,
And in whose spirit there is no guile,
nor fraud is found therein.
Body.3:
3When as I did refrain my speech,
and silent was my tongue,
My bones then waxed old, because
I roared all day long.
Body.4:
4For upon me both day and night
thine hand did heavy lie,
So that my moisture turned is
in summer's drought thereby.
Body.5:
5I thereupon have unto thee
my sin acknowledged,
And likewise mine iniquity
I have not covered:
Body.6:
6I will confess unto the LORD
my trespasses, said I;
And of my sin thou freely didst
forgive th' iniquity.
Body.7:
7For this shall ev'ry godly one
his prayer make to thee;
In such a time he shall thee seek,
as found thou mayest be.
Body.8:
8Surely, when floods of waters great
do swell up to the brim,
They shall not overwhelm his soul,
nor once come near to him.
Body.9:
9Thou art my hiding-place, thou shalt
from trouble keep me free;
Thou with songs of deliverance
about shalt compass me.
Body.10:
10I will instruct thee, and thee teach
the way that thou shalt go;
And, with mine eye upon thee set,
I will direction show.
Body.11:
11Then be not like the horse or mule,
which do not understand;
Whose mouth, lest they come near to thee,
a bridle must command.
Body.12:
12Unto the man that wicked is
his sorrows shall abound;
But him that trusteth in the LORD
mercy shall compass round.
Body.13:
13Ye righteous, in the LORD be glad,
in him do ye rejoice:
All ye that upright are in heart,
for joy lift up your voice.

Body.1:
1Ye righteous, in the LORD rejoice;
it comely is and right,
That upright men, with thankful voice,
should praise the Lord of might.
Body.2:
2Praise GOD with harp, and unto him
sing with the psaltery;
Upon a ten-stringed instrument
make ye sweet melody.
Body.3:
3A new song to him sing, and play
with loud noise skilfully;
For right is GOD's word, all his works
are done in verity.
Body.4:
4To judgment and to righteousness
a love he beareth still;
The loving-kindness of the LORD
the earth throughout doth fill.
Body.5:
5The heavens by the word of GOD
did their beginning take;
And by the breathing of his mouth
he all their hosts did make.
Body.6:
6The waters of the seas he brings
together as an heap;
And in storehouses, as it were,
he layeth up the deep.
Body.7:
7Let earth, and all that live therein,
with rev'rence fear the LORD;
Let all the world's inhabitants
dread him with one accord.
Body.8:
8For he did speak the word, and done
it was without delay;
Established it firmly stood,
whatever he did say.
Body.9:
9GOD doth the counsel bring to nought
which heathen folk do take;
And what the people do devise
of none effect doth make.
Body.10:
10O but the counsel of the LORD
doth stand for ever sure;
And of his heart the purposes
from age to age endure.
Body.11:
11That nation blessed is, whose God
JEHOVAH is, and those
A blessed people are, whom for
his heritage he chose.
Body.12:
12The LORD from heav'n sees and beholds
all sons of men full well:
He views all from his dwelling-place
that in the earth do dwell.
Body.13:
13He forms their hearts alike, and all
their doings he observes.
Great hosts save not a king, much strength
no mighty man preserves.
Body.14:
14An horse for preservation
is a deceitful thing;
And by the greatness of his strength
can no deliv'rance bring.
Body.15:
15Behold, on those that do him fear
the LORD doth set his eye;
Ev'n those who on his mercy do
with confidence rely.
Body.16:
16From death to free their soul, in dearth
life unto them to yield.
Our soul doth wait upon the LORD;
he is our help and shield.
Body.17:
17Sith in his holy name we trust,
our heart shall joyful be.
LORD, let thy mercy be on us,
as we do hope in thee.

Body.1:
1GOD will I bless all times; his praise
my mouth shall still express.
My soul shall boast in GOD: the meek
shall hear with joyfulness.
Body.2:
2Extol the LORD with me, let us
exalt his name together.
I sought the LORD, he heard, and did
me from all fears deliver.
Body.3:
3They looked to him, and lightened were:
not shamed were their faces.
This poor man cried, GOD heard, and saved
him from all his distresses.
Body.4:
4The angel of the LORD encamps,
and round encompasseth
All those about that do him fear,
and them delivereth.
Body.5:
5O taste and see that GOD is good:
who trusts in him is blessed.
Fear GOD his saints: none that him fear
shall be with want oppressed.
Body.6:
6The lions young may hungry be,
and they may lack their food:
But they that truly seek the LORD
shall not lack any good.
Body.7:
7O children, hither do ye come,
and unto me give ear;
I shall you teach to understand
how ye the LORD should fear.
Body.8:
8What man is he that life desires,
to see good would live long?
Thy lips refrain from speaking guile,
and from ill words thy tongue.
Body.9:
9Depart from ill, do good, seek peace,
pursue it earnestly.
GOD's eyes are on the just; his ears
are open to their cry.
Body.10:
10The face of GOD is set against
those that do wickedly,
That he may quite out from the earth
cut off their memory.
Body.11:
11The righteous cry unto the LORD,
he unto them gives ear;
And they out of their troubles all
by him delivered are.
Body.12:
12The LORD is ever nigh to them
that be of broken spirit;
To them he safety doth afford
that are in heart contrite.
Body.13:
13The troubles that afflict the just
in number many be;
But yet at length out of them all
the LORD doth set him free.
Body.14:
14He carefully his bones doth keep,
whatever can befall;
That not so much as one of them
can broken be at all.
Body.15:
15Ill shall the wicked slay; laid waste
shall be who hate the just.
The LORD redeems his servants' souls;
none perish that him trust.

Body.1:
1Plead, LORD, with those that plead; and fight
with those that fight with me.
Of shield and buckler take thou hold,
stand up mine help to be.
Body.2:
2Draw also out the spear, and do
against them stop the way
That me pursue: unto my soul,
I'm thy salvation, say.
Body.3:
3Let them confounded be and shamed
that for my soul have sought:
Who plot my hurt turned back be they,
and to confusion brought.
Body.4:
4Let them be like unto the chaff
that flies before the wind;
And let the angel of the LORD
pursue them hard behind.
Body.5:
5With darkness cover thou their way,
and let it slipp'ry prove;
And let the angel of the LORD
pursue them from above.
Body.6:
6For without cause have they for me
their net hid in a pit,
They also have without a cause
for my soul digged it.
Body.7:
7Let ruin seize him unawares;
his net he hid withal
Himself let catch; and in the same
destruction let him fall.
Body.8:
8My soul in GOD shall joy; and glad
in his salvation be:
And all my bones shall say, O LORD,
who is like unto thee,
Body.9:
9Which dost the poor set free from him
that is for him too strong;
The poor and needy from the man
that spoils and does him wrong?
Body.10:
10False witnesses rose; to my charge
things I not knew they laid.
They, to the spoiling of my soul,
me ill for good repaid.
Body.11:
11But as for me, when they were sick,
in sackcloth sad I mourned:
My humbled soul did fast, my prayer
into my bosom turned.
Body.12:
12Myself I did behave as he
had been my friend or brother;
I heavily bowed down, as one
that mourneth for his mother.
Body.13:
13But in my trouble they rejoiced,
gath'ring themselves together;
Yea, abjects vile together did
themselves against me gather:
Body.14:
14I knew it not; they did me tear,
and quiet would not be.
With mocking hypocrites, at feasts
they gnashed their teeth at me.
Body.15:
15How long, Lord, look'st thou on? from those
destructions they intend
Rescue my soul, from lions young
my darling do defend.
Body.16:
16I will give thanks to thee, O Lord,
within th' assembly great;
And where much people gathered are
thy praises forth will set.
Body.17:
17Let not my wrongful enemies
proudly rejoice o'er me;
Nor who me hate without a cause,
let them wink with the eye.
Body.18:
18For peace they do not speak at all;
but crafty plots prepare
Against all those within the land
that meek and quiet are.
Body.19:
19With mouths set wide, they 'gainst me said,
Ha, ha! our eye doth see.
LORD, thou hast seen, hold not thy peace;
Lord, be not far from me.
Body.20:
20Stir up thyself; wake, that thou may'st
judgment to me afford,
Ev'n to my cause, O thou that art
my only God and Lord.
Body.21:
21O LORD my God, do thou me judge
after thy righteousness;
And let them not their joy 'gainst me
triumphantly express:
Body.22:
22Nor let them say within their hearts,
Ah, we would have it thus;
Nor suffer them to say, that he
is swallowed up by us.
Body.23:
23Shamed and confounded be they all
that at my hurt are glad;
Let those against me that do boast
with shame and scorn be clad.
Body.24:
24Let them that love my righteous cause
be glad, shout, and not cease
To say, The LORD be magnified,
who loves his servant's peace.
Body.25:
25Thy righteousness shall also be
declared by my tongue;
The praises that belong to thee
speak shall it all day long.

Body.1:
1The wicked man's transgression
within my heart thus says,
Undoubtedly the fear of God
is not before his eyes.
Body.2:
2Because himself he flattereth
in his own blinded eye,
Until the hatefulness be found
of his iniquity.
Body.3:
3Words from his mouth proceeding are,
fraud and iniquity:
He to be wise, and to do good,
hath left off utterly.
Body.4:
4He mischief, lying on his bed,
most cunningly doth plot:
He sets himself in ways not good,
ill he abhorreth not.
Body.6:
6LORD, thou preservest man and beast.
How precious is thy grace!
Therefore in shadow of thy wings
men's sons their trust shall place.
Body.7:
7They with the fatness of thy house
shall be well satisfied;
From rivers of thy pleasures thou
wilt drink to them provide.
Body.8:
8Because of life the fountain pure
remains alone with thee;
And in that purest light of thine
we clearly light shall see.
Body.9:
9Thy loving-kindness unto them
continue that thee know;
And still on men upright in heart
thy righteousness bestow.
Body.10:
10Let not the foot of cruel pride
come, and against me stand;
And let me not removed be,
Lord, by the wicked's hand.
Body.11:
11There fall'n are they, and ruined,
that work iniquities:
Cast down they are, and never shall
be able to arise.

Body.1:
1For evildoers fret thou not
thyself unquietly;
Nor do thou envy bear to those
that work iniquity.
Body.2:
2For, even like unto the grass,
soon be cut down shall they;
And, like the green and tender herb,
they wither shall away.
Body.3:
3Set thou thy trust upon the LORD,
and be thou doing good;
And so thou in the land shalt dwell,
and verily have food.
Body.4:
4Delight thyself in GOD; he'll give
thine heart's desire to thee.
Thy way to GOD commit, him trust,
it bring to pass shall he.
Body.5:
5And, like unto the light, he shall
thy righteousness display;
And he thy judgment shall bring forth
like noon-tide of the day.
Body.6:
6Rest in the LORD, and patiently
wait for him: do not fret
For him who, prosp'ring in his way,
success in sin doth get.
Body.7:
7Do thou from anger cease, and wrath
see thou forsake also:
Fret not thyself in any wise,
that evil thou should'st do.
Body.8:
8For those that evildoers are
shall be cut off and fall:
But those that wait upon the LORD
the earth inherit shall.
Body.9:
9For yet a little while, and then
the wicked shall not be;
His place thou shalt consider well,
but it thou shalt not see.
Body.10:
10But by inheritance the earth
the meek ones shall possess:
They also shall delight themselves
in an abundant peace.
Body.11:
11The wicked plots against the just,
and at him whets his teeth:
The Lord shall laugh at him, because
his day he coming seeth.
Body.12:
12The wicked have drawn out the sword,
and bent their bow, to slay
The poor and needy, and to kill
men of an upright way.
Body.13:
13But their own sword, which they have drawn,
shall enter their own heart:
Their bows which they have bent shall break,
and into pieces part.
Body.14:
14A little that a just man hath
is more and better far
Than is the wealth of many such
as lewd and wicked are.
Body.15:
15For sinners' arms shall broken be;
but GOD the just sustains.
GOD knows the just man's days, and still
their heritage remains.
Body.16:
16They shall not be ashamed when they
the evil time do see;
And when the days of famine are,
they satisfied shall be.
Body.17:
17But wicked men, and foes of GOD,
as fat of lambs, decay;
They shall consume, yea, into smoke
they shall consume away.
Body.18:
18The wicked borrows, but the same
again he doth not pay;
Whereas the righteous mercy shows,
and gives his own away.
Body.19:
19For such as blessed be of him
the earth inherit shall;
And they that cursed are of him
shall be destroyed all.
Body.20:
20A good man's footsteps by the LORD
are ordered aright;
And in the way wherein he walks
he greatly doth delight.
Body.21:
21Although he fall, yet shall he not
be cast down utterly,
Because the LORD with his own hand
upholds him mightily.
Body.22:
22I have been young, and now am old,
yet have I never seen
The just man left, nor that his seed
for bread have beggars been.
Body.23:
23He's ever merciful, and lends:
his seed is blessed therefore.
Depart from evil, and do good,
and dwell for evermore.
Body.24:
24For GOD loves judgment, and his saints
leaves not in any case;
They are kept ever; but cut off
shall be the sinner's face.
Body.25:
25The just inherit shall the land,
and ever in it dwell:
The just man's mouth doth wisdom speak;
his tongue doth judgment tell.
Body.26:
26In 's heart the law is of his God,
his steps slide not away.
The wicked man doth watch the just,
and seeketh him to slay.
Body.27:
27Yet him the LORD will not forsake,
nor leave him in his hands:
The righteous will he not condemn,
when he in judgment stands.
Body.28:
28Wait on the LORD, and keep his way,
and thee exalt shall he
Th' earth to inherit; when cut off
the wicked thou shalt see.
Body.29:
29I saw the wicked great in power,
spread like a green bay-tree:
He passed, yea, was not; him I sought,
but found he could not be.
Body.30:
30Mark thou the perfect, and behold
the man of uprightness,
Because that surely of this man
the latter end is peace.
Body.31:
31But those men that transgressors are
shall be destroyed together;
The latter end of wicked men
shall be cut off for ever.
Body.32:
32But the salvation of the just
is from the LORD above;
He in the time of their distress
their stay and strength doth prove.
Body.33:
33The LORD shall help, and them deliver:
he shall them free and save
From wicked men, because in him
their confidence they have.

Body.1:
1In thy great indignation,
O LORD, rebuke me not;
Nor on me lay thy chast'ning hand,
in thy displeasure hot.
Body.2:
2For in me fast thine arrows stick,
thine hand doth press me sore:
And in my flesh there is no health,
nor soundness any more.
Body.3:
3This grief I have, because thy wrath
is forth against me gone;
And in my bones there is no rest,
for sin that I have done.
Body.4:
4Because gone up above mine head
my great transgressions be;
And, as a weighty burden, they
too heavy are for me.
Body.6:
6For a disease that loathsome is
so fills my loins with pain,
That in my weak and weary flesh
no soundness doth remain.
Body.7:
7So feeble and infirm am I,
and broken am so sore,
That, through disquiet of my heart,
I have been made to roar.
Body.8:
8O Lord, all that I do desire
is still before thine eye;
And of my heart the secret groans
not hidden are from thee.
Body.9:
9My heart doth pant incessantly,
my strength doth quite decay;
As for mine eyes, their wonted light
is from me gone away.
Body.10:
10My lovers and my friends do stand
at distance from my sore;
And those do stand aloof that were
kinsmen and kind before.
Body.11:
11Yea, they that seek my life lay snares:
who seek to do me wrong
Speak things mischievous, and deceits
imagine all day long.
Body.12:
12But, as one deaf, that heareth not,
I suffered all to pass;
I as a dumb man did become,
whose mouth not opened was:
Body.13:
13As one that hears not, in whose mouth
are no reproofs at all.
For, LORD, I hope in thee; my God,
thou'lt hear me when I call.
Body.14:
14For I said, Hear me, lest they should
rejoice o'er me with pride;
And o'er me magnify themselves,
when as my foot doth slide.
Body.15:
15For I am near to halt, my grief
is still before mine eye:
For I'll declare my sin, and grieve
for mine iniquity.
Body.16:
16But yet mine en'mies lively are,
and strong are they beside;
And they that hate me wrongfully
are greatly multiplied.
Body.17:
17And they for good that render ill,
as en'mies me withstood;
Yea, ev'n for this, because that I
do follow what is good.
Body.18:
18Forsake me not, O LORD; my God,
far from me never be.
O Lord, thou my salvation art,
haste to give help to me.

Body.1:
1I said, I will look to my ways,
lest with my tongue I sin:
In sight of wicked men my mouth
with bridle I'll keep in.
Body.2:
2With silence I as dumb became,
I did myself restrain
From speaking good; but then the more
increased was my pain.
Body.3:
3My heart within me waxed hot;
and, while I musing was,
The fire did burn; and from my tongue
these words I did let pass:
Body.4:
4Mine end, and measure of my days,
O LORD, unto me show
What is the same; that I thereby
my frailty well may know.
Body.5:
5Lo, thou my days an handbreadth mad'st;
mine age is in thine eye
As nothing: sure each man at best
is wholly vanity.
Body.6:
6Sure each man walks in a vain show;
they vex themselves in vain:
He heaps up wealth, and doth not know
to whom it shall pertain.
Body.7:
7And now, O Lord, what wait I for?
my hope is fixed on thee.
Free me from all my trespasses,
the fool's scorn make not me.
Body.8:
8Dumb was I, op'ning not my mouth,
because this work was thine.
Thy stroke take from me; by the blow
of thine hand I do pine.
Body.9:
9When with rebukes thou dost correct
man for iniquity,
Thou wastes his beauty like a moth:
sure each man's vanity.
Body.10:
10Attend my cry, LORD, at my tears
and pray'rs not silent be:
I sojourn as my fathers all,
and stranger am with thee.
Body.11:
11O spare thou me, that I my strength
recover may again,
Before from hence I do depart,
and here no more remain.

Body.1:
1I waited for the LORD my God,
and patiently did bear;
At length to me he did incline
my voice and cry to hear.
Body.2:
2He took me from a fearful pit,
and from the miry clay,
And on a rock he set my feet,
establishing my way.
Body.3:
3He put a new song in my mouth,
our God to magnify:
Many shall see it, and shall fear,
and on the LORD rely.
Body.4:
4O blessed is the man whose trust
upon the LORD relies;
Respecting not the proud, nor such
as turn aside to lies.
Body.5:
5O LORD my God, full many are
the wonders thou hast done;
Thy gracious thoughts to us-ward far
above all thoughts are gone:
Body.6:
6In order none can reckon them
to thee: if them declare,
And speak of them I would, they more
than can be numbered are.
Body.7:
7No sacrifice nor offering
didst thou at all desire;
Mine ears thou bored: sin-off'ring thou
and burnt didst not require:
Body.8:
8Then to the Lord these were my words,
I come, behold and see;
Within the volume of the book
it written is of me:
Body.9:
9To do thy will I take delight,
O thou my God that art;
Yea, that most holy law of thine
I have within my heart.
Body.10:
10Within the congregation great
I righteousness did preach:
Lo, thou dost know, O LORD, that I
refrained not my speech.
Body.11:
11I never did within my heart
conceal thy righteousness;
I thy salvation have declared,
and shown thy faithfulness:
Body.12:
12Thy kindness, which most loving is,
concealed have not I,
Nor from the congregation great
have hid thy verity.
Body.13:
13Thy tender mercies, LORD, from me
O do thou not restrain;
Thy loving-kindness, and thy truth,
let them me still maintain.
Body.14:
14For ills past reck'ning compass me,
and mine iniquities
Such hold upon me taken have,
I cannot lift mine eyes:
Body.15:
15They more than hairs are on mine head,
thence is my heart dismayed.
Be pleased, LORD, to rescue me;
LORD, hasten to mine aid.
Body.16:
16Shamed and confounded be they all
that seek my soul to kill;
Yea, let them backward driven be,
and shamed, that wish me ill.
Body.17:
17For a reward of this their shame
confounded let them be,
That in this manner scoffing say,
Aha, aha! to me.
Body.18:
18In thee let all be glad, and joy,
who seeking thee abide;
Who thy salvation love, say still,
The LORD be magnified.
Body.19:
19I'm poor and needy, yet the Lord
of me a care doth take:
Thou art my help and saviour,
my God, no tarrying make.

Body.1:
1Blessed is he that wisely doth
the poor man's case consider;
For when the time of trouble is,
the LORD will him deliver.
Body.3:
3GOD will give strength when he on bed
of languishing doth mourn;
And in his sickness sore, O LORD,
thou all his bed wilt turn.
Body.4:
4I said, O LORD, do thou extend
thy mercy unto me;
O do thou heal my soul; for why?
I have offended thee.
Body.5:
5Those that to me are enemies,
of me do evil say,
When shall he die, that so his name
may perish quite away?
Body.6:
6To see me if he comes, he speaks
vain words: but then his heart
Heaps mischief to it, which he tells,
when forth he doth depart.
Body.7:
7My haters jointly whispering,
'gainst me my hurt devise.
Mischief, say they, cleaves fast to him;
he lieth, and shall not rise.
Body.8:
8Yea, ev'n mine own familiar friend,
on whom I did rely,
Who ate my bread, ev'n he his heel
against me lifted high.
Body.9:
9But, LORD, be merciful to me,
and up again me raise,
That I may justly them requite
according to their ways.
Body.10:
10By this I know that certainly
I favoured am by thee;
Because my hateful enemy
triumphs not over me.
Body.11:
11But as for me, thou me uphold'st
in mine integrity;
And me before thy countenance
thou sett'st continually.
Body.12:
12The LORD, the God of Israel,
be blessed for ever then,
From age to age eternally.
Amen, yea, and amen.

Body.1:
1Like as the hart for water-brooks
in thirst doth pant and bray;
So pants my longing soul, O God,
that come to thee I may.
Body.2:
2My soul for God, the living God,
doth thirst: when shall I near
Unto thy countenance approach,
and in God's sight appear?
Body.3:
3My tears have unto me been meat,
both in the night and day,
While unto me continually,
Where is thy God? they say.
Body.4:
4My soul is poured out in me,
when this I think upon;
Because that with the multitude
I heretofore had gone:
Body.5:
5With them into God's house I went,
with voice of joy and praise;
Yea, with the multitude that kept
the solemn holy days.
Body.6:
6O why art thou cast down, my soul?
why in me so dismayed?
Trust God, for I shall praise him yet,
his count'nance is mine aid.
Body.7:
7My God, my soul's cast down in me;
thee therefore mind I will
From Jordan's land, the Hermonites,
and ev'n from Mizar hill.
Body.8:
8At the noise of thy water-spouts
deep unto deep doth call;
Thy breaking waves pass over me,
yea, and thy billows all.
Body.9:
9His loving-kindness yet the LORD
command will in the day,
His song's with me by night; to God,
by whom I live, I'll pray:
Body.10:
10And I will say to God my rock,
Why me forgett'st thou so?
Why, for my foes' oppression,
thus mourning do I go?
Body.11:
11'Tis as a sword within my bones,
when my foes me upbraid;
Ev'n when by them, Where is thy God?
'tis daily to me said.
Body.12:
12O why art thou cast down, my soul?
why, thus with grief oppressed,
Art thou disquieted in me?
in God still hope and rest:
Body.13:
13For yet I know I shall him praise,
who graciously to me
The health is of my countenance,
yea, mine own God is he.

Body.1:
1Judge me, O God, and plead my cause
against th' ungodly nation;
From the unjust and crafty man,
O be thou my salvation.
Body.2:
2For thou the God art of my strength;
why thrusts thou me thee fro'?
For th' enemy's oppression
why do I mourning go?
Body.4:
4Then will I to God's altar go,
to God my chiefest joy:
Yea, God, my God, thy name to praise
my harp I will employ.
Body.5:
5Why art thou then cast down, my soul?
what should discourage thee?
And why with vexing thoughts art thou
disquieted in me?
Body.6:
6Still trust in God; for him to praise
good cause I yet shall have:
He of my count'nance is the health,
my God that doth me save.

Body.1:
1O God, we with our ears have heard,
our fathers have us told,
What works thou in their days hadst done,
ev'n in the days of old.
Body.2:
2Thy hand did drive the heathen out,
and plant them in their place;
Thou didst afflict the nations,
but them thou didst increase.
Body.4:
4Thou art my King: for Jacob, Lord,
deliv'rances command.
Through thee we shall push down our foes,
that do against us stand:
Body.5:
5We, through thy name, shall tread down those
that ris'n against us have.
For in my bow I shall not trust,
nor shall my sword me save.
Body.6:
6But from our foes thou hast us saved,
our haters put to shame.
In God we all the day do boast,
and ever praise thy name.
Body.7:
7But now we are cast off by thee,
and us thou putt'st to shame;
And when our armies do go forth,
thou goest not with the same.
Body.8:
8Thou mak'st us from the enemy,
faint-hearted, to turn back;
And they who hate us for themselves
our spoils away do take.
Body.10:
10Thou mak'st us a reproach to be
unto our neighbours near;
Derision and a scorn to them
that round about us are.
Body.11:
11A by-word also thou dost us
among the heathen make;
The people, in contempt and spite,
at us their heads do shake.
Body.12:
12Before me my confusion
continually abides;
And of my bashful countenance
the shame me ever hides:
Body.13:
13For voice of him that doth reproach,
and speaketh blasphemy;
By reason of th' avenging foe,
and cruel enemy.
Body.14:
14All this is come on us, yet we
have not forgotten thee;
Nor falsely in thy covenant
behaved ourselves have we.
Body.16:
16If we God's name forgot, or stretched
to a strange god our hands,
Shall not God search this out? for he
heart's secrets understands.
Body.17:
17Yea, for thy sake we're killed all day,
counted as slaughter-sheep.
Rise, Lord, cast us not ever off;
awake, why dost thou sleep?
Body.18:
18O wherefore hidest thou thy face?
forgett'st our cause distressed,
And our oppression? For our soul
is to the dust down pressed:
Body.19:
19Our belly also on the earth
fast cleaving, hold doth take.
Rise for our help, and us redeem,
ev'n for thy mercies' sake.

Body.1:
1My heart brings forth a goodly thing;
my words that I indite
Concern the King: my tongue's a pen
of one that swift doth write.
Body.2:
2Thou fairer art than sons of men:
into thy lips is store
Of grace infused; God therefore thee
hath blessed for evermore.
Body.3:
3O thou that art the mighty One,
thy sword gird on thy thigh;
Ev'n with thy glory excellent,
and with thy majesty.
Body.4:
4For meekness, truth, and righteousness,
in state ride prosp'rously;
And thy right hand shall thee instruct
in things that fearful be.
Body.5:
5Thine arrows sharply pierce the heart
of th' en'mies of the King;
And under thy subjection
the people down do bring.
Body.6:
6For ever and for ever is,
O God, thy throne of might;
The sceptre of thy kingdom is
a sceptre that is right.
Body.8:
8Of aloes, myrrh, and cassia,
a smell thy garments had,
Out of the iv'ry palaces,
whereby they made thee glad.
Body.9:
9Among thy women hon'rable
kings' daughters were at hand:
Upon thy right hand did the queen
in gold of Ophir stand.
Body.10:
10O daughter, hearken and regard,
and do thine ear incline;
Likewise forget thy father's house,
and people that are thine.
Body.11:
11Then of the King desired shall be
thy beauty veh'mently:
Because he is thy Lord, do thou
him worship rev'rently.
Body.12:
12The daughter there of Tyre shall be
with gifts and off'rings great:
Those of the people that are rich
thy favour shall entreat.
Body.13:
13Behold, the daughter of the King
all glorious is within;
And with embroideries of gold
her garments wrought have been.
Body.14:
14She shall be brought unto the King
in robes with needle wrought;
Her fellow-virgins following
shall unto thee be brought.
Body.15:
15They shall be brought with gladness great,
and mirth on ev'ry side,
Into the palace of the King,
and there they shall abide.
Body.16:
16Instead of those thy fathers dear,
thy children thou may'st take,
And in all places of the earth
them noble princes make.
Body.17:
17Thy name remembered I will make
through ages all to be:
The people therefore evermore
shall praises give to thee.

Body.1:
1My heart inditing is
good matter in a song:
I speak the things that I have made,
which to the King belong:
Body.2:
2My tongue shall be as quick,
his honour to indite,
As is the pen of any scribe
that useth fast to write.
Body.3:
3Thou 'rt fairest of all men;
grace in thy lips doth flow:
And therefore blessings evermore
on thee doth God bestow.
Body.4:
4Thy sword gird on thy thigh,
thou that art most of might:
Appear in dreadful majesty,
and in thy glory bright.
Body.5:
5For meekness, truth, and right,
ride prosp'rously in state;
And thy right hand shall teach to thee
things terrible and great.
Body.6:
6Thy shafts shall pierce their hearts
that foes are to the King;
Whereby into subjection
the people thou shalt bring.
Body.7:
7Thy royal seat, O Lord,
for ever shall remain:
The sceptre of thy kingdom doth
all righteousness maintain.
Body.9:
9Of myrrh and spices sweet
a smell thy garments had,
Out of the iv'ry palaces,
whereby they made thee glad.
Body.10:
10And in thy glorious train
kings' daughters waiting stand;
And thy fair queen, in Ophir gold,
doth stand at thy right hand.
Body.11:
11O daughter, take good heed,
incline, and give good ear;
Thou must forget thy kindred all,
and father's house most dear.
Body.12:
12Thy beauty to the King
shall then delightful be:
And do thou humbly worship him,
because thy Lord is he.
Body.13:
13The daughter then of Tyre
there with a gift shall be,
And all the wealthy of the land
shall make their suit to thee.
Body.14:
14The daughter of the King
all glorious is within;
And with embroideries of gold
her garments wrought have been.
Body.15:
15She cometh to the King
in robes with needle wrought;
The virgins that do follow her
shall unto thee be brought.
Body.16:
16They shall be brought with joy,
and mirth on ev'ry side,
Into the palace of the King,
and there they shall abide.
Body.17:
17And in thy fathers' stead,
thy children thou may'st take,
And in all places of the earth
them noble princes make.
Body.18:
18I will show forth thy name
to generations all:
Therefore the people evermore
to thee give praises shall.

Body.1:
1God is our refuge and our strength,
in straits a present aid;
Therefore, although the earth remove,
we will not be afraid:
Body.2:
2Though hills amidst the seas be cast;
Though waters roaring make,
And troubled be; yea, though the hills
by swelling seas do shake.
Body.3:
3A river is, whose streams do glad
the city of our God;
The holy place, wherein the Lord
most high hath his abode.
Body.4:
4God in the midst of her doth dwell;
nothing shall her remove:
The Lord to her an helper will,
and that right early, prove.
Body.5:
5The heathen raged tumultuously,
the kingdoms moved were:
The Lord God uttered his voice,
the earth did melt for fear.
Body.6:
6The LORD of hosts upon our side
doth constantly remain:
The God of Jacob's our refuge,
us safely to maintain.
Body.7:
7Come, and behold what wondrous works
have by the LORD been wrought;
Come, see what desolations
he on the earth hath brought.
Body.8:
8Unto the ends of all the earth
wars into peace he turns:
The bow he breaks, the spear he cuts,
in fire the chariot burns.
Body.9:
9Be still, and know that I am God;
among the heathen I
Will be exalted; I on earth
will be exalted high.
Body.10:
10Our God, who is the LORD of hosts,
is still upon our side;
The God of Jacob our refuge
for ever will abide.

Body.1:
1All people, clap your hands; to God
with voice of triumph shout:
For dreadful is the LORD most high,
